messages.content:
Ruby's URI parser accepts `|`, `{`, and `"`, but rejects backslashes, invalid percent-escapes, and raw non-ASCII. Real browsers percent-encode the URLs they send, so the `request.url` deep links the app generates will still parse. Anything that fails to parse should just fall back to the default landing page.

My plan:
- In `SessionsController#create`, only honor `return_to` when it is a string that is either a relative path or an http(s) URL whose host is this request's host. Rebuild the redirect from the path and query alone, and refuse anything starting with `//`, since that becomes off-site.
- Drop `allow_other_host: true`, so Rails' open-redirect guard stays on as a backstop.
- Ignore any value that fails to parse or isn't a string, so sign-in still succeeds and lands on the default page.

class SessionsController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access only: %i[ new create ]
  rate_limit to: 10, within: 3.minutes, only: :create, with: -> { render_rejection :too_many_requests }

  before_action :ensure_user_exists, only: :new

  def new
  end

  def create
    if user = User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: params[:email_address], password: params[:password])
      start_new_session_for user
      redirect_to same_host_return_to || post_authenticating_url
    else
      render_rejection :unauthorized
    end
  end

  def destroy
    terminate_current_session
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def ensure_user_exists
      redirect_to first_run_url if User.none?
    end

    # return_to arrives in shared and emailed links, so it can name any site. Only honor a path on this host,
    # and rebuild the redirect from that path and query. Anything else (another host, a "//" URL, a non-string
    # value, or something unparseable) returns nil so the reader gets the default landing page instead.
    def same_host_return_to
      return_to = params[:return_to]
      return unless return_to.is_a?(String) && return_to.present?

      uri = URI.parse(return_to)
      if uri.scheme || uri.host
        return unless %w[ http https ].include?(uri.scheme&.downcase) && uri.host&.casecmp?(request.host) && uri.userinfo.nil?
      end

      path = uri.path.presence || "/"
      return unless path.start_with?("/") && !path.start_with?("//")

      uri.query.present? ? "#{path}?#{uri.query}" : path
    rescue URI::Error
      nil
    end

    def render_rejection(status)
      flash[:alert] = "Too many requests or unauthorized."
      render :new, status: status
    end
end

The open redirect is closed. `SessionsController#create` now only honors `return_to` when it points at this host, and the full suite is green.

**The cause:** `create` redirected to `params[:return_to]` with `allow_other_host: true` and no check, so any site could be the landing page right after the password was entered.

**The fix** (`app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb`, the only existing file changed):
- `return_to` is honored only if it is a string that is either a relative path or an http(s) URL whose host matches the request's host. The redirect is rebuilt from the path and query, so no other host can ever be the target.
- Anything starting with `//` is refused, since Rails would send it off-site.
- Non-string values (`return_to[]=x`, `return_to[a]=b`), malformed or unparseable values, and URLs with userinfo all fall back to the default landing page. Sign-in still succeeds in every case.
- I removed `allow_other_host: true`, so Rails' own open-redirect guard stays on as a backstop.

**Verification:**
- Same-host deep links work, including query strings, relative paths, and IPv6 hosts. The full signed-out → login form → sign-in round trip lands on the original page.
- `https://evil…`, `//evil…`, `///evil…`, `/\evil…`, `javascript:`, userinfo tricks, and similar all land on root.
- I added `test/controllers/sessions_return_to_test.rb` with 9 tests. They fail against the original controller and pass with the fix. I did not edit any existing test file or `bin/rails`.
- `bin/rails test`: 188 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors. The 2 skips were there before. Rubocop is clean. Nothing under `db/` changed.

**Behavior changes to be aware of:**
- A deep link to a different port on the same host is treated as same-host and redirected to our host and port.
- A deep link with raw non-ASCII characters in it now falls back to the default page. Browsers percent-encode URLs, so real deep links are unaffected.
- A POST with a non-string `return_to` used to raise a 500. It now signs in and goes to root.

The session-stored fallback in `post_authenticating_url` (`return_to_after_authenticating`) is untouched. Nothing in this repo writes to it, so it is not attacker-controllable here.
